body:
<!-- repo-rationalization:2026-10-10:audit -->

Owner-authorized single documentation reconciliation task. Do this audit before implementation intake. Use code-change-v1 to produce a reviewed documentation PR; do not create child/implementation jobs or implement code/runtime changes.

Coordinator: https://github.com/Khamel83/kid-friendly-ai/issues/34

Read AGENTS, CHARTER when present, TODO, CONTEXT, HANDOFF and INFRA from the fetched default branch. Preserve dirty/unpublished work. Reuse the existing canonical plan; create docs/REPO_PLAN.md only if no suitable plan exists. Correct verified current records and preserve historical evidence.

- [ ] Account for every visible outstanding TODO and open issue/PR with stable source links; check recent merged/closed evidence for claimed completion. G2K captures native issue/PR inputs in this same audit worktree before model execution at docs/reconciliation/intake-2026-10-10.json and its hashed parts. Read all parts and the manifest; record omitted or unreadable coverage explicitly. Never invent evidence or access credentials.
- [ ] Classify items as completed, remaining, duplicate/superseded, blocked/owner decision or unknown. Completion must meet its own criteria; use owning deployment receipts and downstream readback when required. Source-only success is not runtime acceptance.
- [ ] Produce one coherent ordered plan with dependencies, owner decisions, acceptance criteria and proposed native issue dispositions. Link the coordinator and keep task prose in its owning records.
- [ ] Update TODO, CONTEXT and HANDOFF to the verified result. In the PR, report captured source revisions, readable/missing inputs and exact coverage. Keep unknowns and unresolved acceptance open. Do not close unrelated issues, change lifecycle/access/repair policy or enqueue implementation. The coordinator stays tracking-only.

Stage: ready for the deployed G2K native capture and documentation audit contract.

Skill hint: code-change-v1

After trusted exact-head plan review and merge, the owner authorizes G2K to link existing ready issues and admit one finite batch for uncovered ready jobs through its ready-jobs contract. The audit model does not enqueue work or change code/runtime. Keep the coordinator parked/tracking-only.

title: docs: project owner-approved all-PR PASS merge policy
body:
## Summary

```text
AGENTS.md managed blocks → current approved shared rules
```

This PR projects the owner-approved expansion of merge eligibility to all PR types and the current shared working-document rules into managed `AGENTS.md` blocks. The policy expansion is intentional. Project-owned text outside managed blocks is preserved byte-for-byte.

Repository base before this projection: `8947fc3ac0078b38bac5dea9c2ec7fc7e651f39e`
- [Prior AGENTS.md](https://github.com/Khamel83/kid-friendly-ai/blob/8947fc3ac0078b38bac5dea9c2ec7fc7e651f39e/AGENTS.md)

The base identifies the input document, not the source of the updated policy. Homelab owns private shared rules and repository membership; Janitor publishes its working-document and public-source rules.

## Explicit owner authorization and policy scope

The repository owner explicitly approved this policy in the agent task that produced this repair. The owner's instruction was: “I meant every PR with a bot pass would merge.” The owner also specified: “If it's an active repository that we haven't excluded for whatever reason, it should apply to.” The owner subsequently authorized completion of the work. This is an out-of-band owner instruction: the private conversation cannot be independently verified from this public repository. This PR description records that limitation explicitly; historical implementation links are not substitutes for the owner's decision.

The all-PR eligibility change is intentional and owner-approved, including removal of author, label and changed-path restrictions on **merging**. It does not authorize an agent to create, deploy, execute, send or activate unrelated work. GitHub's required checks and branch protections remain enforced by the normal SHA-pinned merge endpoint. A task that includes deployment still needs its own deployment authority; this AGENTS-only projection does not deploy any runtime.

Homelab's private `config/project-catalog.yml` is the central authority for active repository membership and explicit merge exclusions. Janitor reads that catalog before selecting repositories; a repository-local copy is deliberately not authoritative and is not published here. Local agents should use the existing standing Janitor worker, not infer fleet membership or exclusions from this public document. Homelab owns reviewer/PASS improvements; Janitor consumes that verdict and records the merge outcome. No second local reviewer or policy registry is introduced.

The working-document link in AGENTS.md intentionally follows the approved contract on the docs repository's `main` branch. That link is a live policy pointer, not an immutable snapshot. The pinned source below records the version used to produce this projection; future approved contract updates are intended to remain discoverable through the live pointer.

## Evidence

- **Before:** old policy projection `5a5045f9f1ea6a49eef68aa1f9511cd2a5408193`.
  **After:** exact current managed blocks at `7a89622027db8c8268cd76bcd55b8ab90a375cd9`.
- The owner explicitly approved every PR type after current-head trusted OCI bot PASS; this records that existing decision rather than proposing a new permission.
- The working-document contract used for this projection is pinned at [docs PR85 source](https://github.com/Khamel83/docs/blob/0cf0fbf847d5afe0b50f6db47a7519df2ad09fad/templates/WORKING_DOCUMENTS.md). Its main-branch pointer intentionally follows future approved upkeep policy.
- Exact renderer equality, repeat-render idempotence, byte-for-byte preservation of text outside managed blocks, AGENTS-only changed paths and `git diff --check` pass.
- Public repositories receive only the public-safe profile. No private shared-rule block is copied into them.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** merge-policy projection

The policy governs merging; it grants no authority to create, deploy, send, file, or activate work beyond existing project authorization. Project-specific restrictions remain byte-for-byte intact.

title: Validate generated Next declaration through guarded release copy
body:
## Summary

Buddy prepare currently builds and passes its keyless probe, then refuses Next.js's ignored generated next-env.d.ts. Accept only the exact Next14.0.4 declaration after the build and revalidate it in the root-owned copy before publication.

```text
clean source → locked build → exact generated declaration → root copy recheck → publish
```

All other ignored files remain refused. Safe leaf checks cover single-link regular files, no-follow/nonblocking opens, bounds and pre/post identity. Missing safe-open support fails closed.

## Evidence

- **Before:** PR25's installed reviewed operator refused the generated declaration before publication; the dirty active checkout and servicePID1204 were preserved.
  **After:** 54 release tests pass, including independent generator-output fixture bytes, mutation during root copy, dependency-location mismatch refusal and bounded multi-chunk reads, with no publication and exact staging cleanup. Compilation and diff checks pass.
- Separately, parent invoked the actual installed Next14.0.4 generator on OCI in disposable private scratch: its201-byte output matched the canonical declaration (SHA9269d492). Generator source hash and cleanup are recorded in docs/NEXT_GENERATOR_EVIDENCE.md. The unit test itself is an independent literal fixture comparison.
- PR25 is the historical accepted operator. This PR26 repair has independent production PASS and passing Node CI for its initial head; the final documentation head still needs its own trusted PASS/CI before a fresh operator capsule and guarded prepare/install.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** Buddy

No app/service change occurs from this source commit. Existing source-copy, strict Git verification, credential isolation, CAS install and rollback guards remain in force.

title: feat: release Buddy on OCI from a verified immutable build
body:
Buddy's active OCI checkout contains unpublished edits and still reports the old memory-health failure. This adds a Buddy-only release operator that prepares the exact fetched, reviewed source into an immutable artifact, then installs it through the existing systemd service while preserving the dirty checkout and native unit.

Root verifies the copied Git metadata and tracked tree independently of the service-user index, using full strict fsck, isolated config and direct blob/mode checks. The manifest binds the verified source. Failure cleans only the owned unpublished stage; published releases survive post-rename failure. Install and rollback use private beforeimages, file/service CAS checks, exact systemd255 environment-file flags and bounded loopback health checks. No provider request or route change is part of the operator.

The privileged bundle is four colocated modules: CLI, primitives, Git verification and state. Test fixtures and prepare tests are split so the complete patch fits the existing reviewer limits. Current validation: 40 release tests, Python compilation, shell syntax and diff checks pass; independent adversarial review passed the production repair. Final-head trusted review and Node18/20 CI remain required before OCI use. Runtime installation, provider response, fencing and recovery/return are separate open gates.

title: Document the optional Apple/container development workflow
body:
Parent issue: #3

## What
Document the Apple/container workflow in `DEVELOPER_GUIDE.md`, while retaining docker-compose.yml for Redis, Nginx, and Linux/systemd deployment. Include prerequisites, installation and service startup, image build, application-image smoke test, environment handling, and known limitations.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The documentation states that Apple silicon and macOS 26 or newer are required.
- [ ] The documentation points to the signed Apple/container release and explains how to start its system service.
- [ ] The documented commands build the existing Dockerfile `runner` target and run the focused application-image smoke test.
- [ ] The documented workflow covers port 3000, `/api/health`, and the AI-independent route check.
- [ ] Secret values are obtained from the developer's environment rather than committed to the repository or copied into scripts.
- [ ] The documentation explicitly says Apple/container is an optional development and validation path, not a replacement for the Docker Compose or Linux/systemd production path.
- [ ] The documentation states that the complete multi-service compose lifecycle, including Redis and Nginx, is not covered by this workflow.

title: Add an Apple/container application-image smoke test
body:
Parent issue: #3

## What
Add a focused smoke-test command for the Apple/container-built application image. Start only the application image, publish host port 3000 to container port 3000, and pass the non-secret environment contract already defined for the docker-compose.yml app service. Wait for startup, exercise `/api/health`, and exercise the application's AI-independent route. Always remove the container on success or failure.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The command accepts the image tag produced by the Apple/container build command.
- [ ] The command starts the image without Redis, Nginx, Docker Compose, or host bind mounts.
- [ ] Only non-secret environment values already required by the compose app service are passed; secrets are not embedded in the script.
- [ ] The command polls until the application is ready and fails on timeout.
- [ ] `GET /api/health` must return the expected successful health response.
- [ ] The selected AI-independent application route must return a successful HTTP response.
- [ ] Any failed request, startup error, or timeout produces a nonzero exit status.
- [ ] Cleanup runs when the smoke test is interrupted or fails.
- [ ] The smoke command is a focused end-to-end check of the OCI image and documents that it must be run on an Apple-silicon macOS 26 host.

title: Build the existing Next.js runner image with Apple/container
body:
Parent issue: #3

## What
Add an optional build command that uses Apple/container to build the repository's existing Dockerfile `runner` target as an OCI image. Reuse the current Dockerfile and build context; do not add a second image definition or require Docker Compose.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The command runs the prerequisite check before attempting a build.
- [ ] The command builds the existing Dockerfile `runner` target with Apple/container.
- [ ] The image tag is configurable and has a documented deterministic default.
- [ ] The command returns a nonzero status and preserves the build error when the image cannot be built.
- [ ] The resulting image exposes the existing application port 3000 and contains the current production runner contents.
- [ ] The existing Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, and Linux/systemd deployment behavior remain unchanged.

title: Add an Apple/container prerequisite check for local app validation
body:
Parent issue: #3

## What
Add a small executable prerequisite check for the optional Apple/container workflow. It must verify that the host is Apple silicon, macOS 26 or newer, and that the `container` CLI is installed and its system service is available. The check must not install software or modify the production Docker/systemd path.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The check rejects non-Darwin and non-arm64 hosts with an actionable error.
- [ ] The check rejects macOS versions below 26 with an actionable error.
- [ ] The check reports how to install the signed Apple/container release when the CLI is missing.
- [ ] The check reports how to start the Apple/container system service when it is unavailable.
- [ ] The check exits successfully when all prerequisites are available.
- [ ] The check can be run independently without Redis, Nginx, Docker Compose, or application secrets.

title: Add local extraction evaluation fixtures and rollout checks
body:
Parent issue: #4

## What
Add a focused evaluation command for the parental-review endpoint using representative bounded conversation fixtures: age-appropriate content, unsafe content, ambiguous wording, multilingual text from the application's supported language set, and repeated phrases occurring in different messages.

Run the fixtures against a configured local Ollama model through the same HTTP contract used in development. The evaluator must validate the response schema and verify that every returned source span is in bounds and that its quote matches the referenced message. For repeated phrases, verify that the reported occurrence is the occurrence identified by the fixture. Produce aggregate results without writing transcripts, prompts, excerpts, or findings to persistent storage.

Document how to run the evaluation locally and keep the production feature flag disabled by default until the evaluation has been reviewed.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The fixture set includes all five required conversation classes and remains within the endpoint's request limit.
- [ ] The evaluator exercises the real HTTP endpoint and reports schema, offset, quote, and repeated-occurrence failures distinctly.
- [ ] Evaluation output contains aggregate pass/fail information only and does not persist or print conversation text or model prompts.
- [ ] The documented command works with the local Ollama configuration and does not require a cloud provider.
- [ ] The default deployment configuration leaves parental-review extraction opt-in and does not change the authoritative real-time safety path.

title: Display grounded parental-review findings in the parental-controls interface
body:
Parent issue: #4

## What
Add a review panel to the existing parental-controls interface using the server-side review result. For each finding, show its category, severity, speaker, explanation, and grounded source quote with the source message location. Make the source quote visibly distinct from the explanation so a parent can tell what came from the conversation versus the extractor.

Provide explicit loading, no-findings, disabled, and unavailable states. Do not expose raw prompts or full transcripts beyond the returned source excerpts. Treat findings as an auditable secondary signal: they must not block, rewrite, or otherwise replace the existing real-time content filter or conversation behavior.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A successful review renders every returned finding with category, severity, speaker, explanation, and source quote.
- [ ] The empty, disabled, loading, and unavailable states are understandable and do not appear as safety approvals.
- [ ] Source quotes are rendered as excerpts tied to their reported message location; the full conversation is not duplicated into the panel.
- [ ] The panel does not alter message delivery, existing content-filter decisions, or normal chat latency.
- [ ] UI checks cover successful findings, no findings, and service-unavailable responses using the repository's existing component-testing conventions.
